text:
**A 200 W panel refills a 1,000 Wh station in about 1.5 days of decent sun. For a full recharge in one day, plan on roughly 300-350 W.**

**The math:** panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charging losses.

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day recharge |
|---|---|
| 3 (shoulder season) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

Source: [Power Station Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). Another guide puts a 1,000 Wh refill at about 300 W in summer and 735 W or more in a northern winter ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Other sizing options:**
- **200 W:** at 4.5 sun hours and 70% efficiency, it puts about 630 Wh a day into the battery, so about 1.5 days to fill from empty ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **100 W:** about 315 Wh a day, so around 3 days.
- **400 W:** about 1,260 Wh a day, so under a day.
- **Quick rule:** capacity in Wh ÷ 5 gives the panel watts for roughly a day and a half of sun.

**Check these before buying:**
1. **Your station's max solar input (watts).** Panels above that limit add nothing, and many 1,000 Wh units accept 200-800 W. Slightly oversizing can help in weak light.
2. **Input voltage range.** A panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside your station's window. Going over can damage the charge controller. Panels wired in series add voltage.
3. **Connector type.** Most panels use MC4, while stations often take XT60 or DC barrel plugs, so you may need an adapter.
4. **Running loads while charging.** Net charging is solar input minus whatever you're drawing.
5. **Winter and clouds.** Use your worst-case sun hours. Solid overcast can cut output by 75% or more.

**A 400 W option if your station can take it:** the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) lists at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (checked by the retailer on 2026-10-21). It has a 45.3 V Voc and MC4 connectors, with XT60 and DC adapters included. It weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), and it's too high-voltage for stations with a 24-28 V input ceiling.
